from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
p=Path('tmp/pdfs'); p.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
print('Pages:',len(r.pages))
texts=[]
for i,page in enumerate(r.pages,1):
 t=page.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout')
 (p/f'page-{i:02}.txt').write_text(t)
 texts.append(f'\\n===== PAGE {i} =====\\n'+t)
(p/'manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n'.join(texts))
print('\\n'.join(texts)[:54000])
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from fractions import Fraction as F
from math import sqrt
x=[F(0),F(1),F(3)]
y=[-v for v in x]
mx=sum(x)/3; my=sum(y)/3
vx=sum((v-mx)**2 for v in x)/3
vy=sum((v-my)**2 for v in y)/3
t=[v+(my-mx) for v in x]
w2=sum((a-b)**2 for a,b in zip(sorted(t),sorted(y)))/3
print('Affine reflection check for X uniform on {0,1,3}:')
print('variance:',vy,'W2 squared:',w2,'affinity:',1-sqrt(float(w2/(2*vy)))))
PY"

strengths: The Gaussian optimal-transport alignment provides an interesting, distribution-sensitive reference for studying activation behavior. Organizing the resulting scores into layerwise signatures is a potentially useful contribution to model analysis.

The empirical survey is substantial, spanning convolutional, residual, NAS-derived, transformer, and modern convolutional architectures on all 50,000 ImageNet validation images. The raw signatures and architecture comparisons reveal informative patterns beyond a single aggregate statistic.

The controlled comparison of plain and residual ResNet20 in Figure 7 provides direct evidence that residual connections affect the measured activation distributions. This is stronger support than comparisons between unrelated pretrained architectures alone.

The appendices include useful checks involving batch size, nine training seeds, alternative input datasets, and supervised/self-supervised checkpoints. The explanatory figures, supplied derivations, and code link also support transparency.
weaknesses: The central interpretation as a measure of functional non-linearity exceeds the mathematical guarantees. Equation (5) compares marginal distributions and discards input–output correspondence. For example, if X is uniform on [0,1], the nonlinear function σ(x)=1−|2x−1| also produces a uniform distribution, giving T_aff=identity and affinity 1. Conversely, Theorem 3.3 establishes recovery for positive-definite linear transformations, rather than arbitrary affine functions. Thus the claimed identification of linearity is not valid in the stated generality.

The connection from activation signatures to whole-network non-linearity or expressivity remains unvalidated. The signature omits nonlinear operations such as input-dependent attention and normalization, and it does not account for composition or cancellation: ReLU(x)−ReLU(−x)=x despite nonlinear hidden activations. Figures 5–6 establish differences in the proposed descriptor, but do not establish the claimed ordering of end-to-end non-linearity or explain transformers’ greater expressive power.

The accuracy analysis in Figure 6 selects the best statistic and fitted relationship separately within small model groups, including only five ViTs, and reports fit quality on those same models. There is no held-out predictive evaluation or controlled separation of architecture, scale, activation choice, and training recipe. The reported R² values support exploratory associations, but provide insufficient evidence for the stronger predictive and explanatory conclusions.

The treatment of alternatives weakens the originality and validation arguments. Remark 3.6 describes T_aff as a globally optimal nonlinear alignment of the activation data, although its optimality concerns the Gaussian approximations. Its criticism of R² also overlooks that an optimized in-sample affine least-squares fit with an intercept has nonnegative R². Section 3.3’s dismissal of Jacobian-based measures because ReLU is nondifferentiable is insufficient, since ReLU networks have Jacobians almost everywhere. Low Pearson correlations with other statistics establish difference, not greater validity as a non-linearity measure.

The implementation introduces transformations whose relationship to the theory needs stronger support. Spatial averaging in Appendix C is not lossless: generally r(σ(X))≠σ(r(X)), and pooled outputs need not be a deterministic function of pooled inputs. Covariance shrinkage also changes the exact covariance-matching premise. Figure 9 provides useful numerical checks but does not establish preservation of architecture rankings. The empirical Wasserstein solver and exact checkpoint choices are also insufficiently specified. Overall, the central definition and validation gaps outweigh the worthwhile descriptive contribution and determine the weak-reject recommendation; presentation refinements are secondary.
